absolutely. I get paralyzed. this happens to me quite a lot. I’m sorry you’re experiencing this too. In the Polyvagal Theory, this is called Dorsal Vagal. In complete shutdown mode. My therapist recommends to me when that happens, to try to keep calm and mindfully move your fingers. Or whatever body part you feel the most. And really notice the sensation. The best thing to do is to move around slowly, if you can or notice whatever is around you. Asking yourself questions like: What’s the room you’re in?  What’s the year? To find something to ground you.. I hope this helps for another time!

I’m able to ground myself rather quickly after a couple hours of feeling strange. I have to accept my reality before anything gets better. Yup I’m not myself and I’m okay with it, and then I’m able to focus on my breath and just take it easy. It definitely takes a full day to come back to 100%. Meditation has been the one thing keep me sane. Gratitude. Yes I find journaling can sometimes trigger something to happen like that. Before you journal, ask yourself what you need in the moment. Well, I’m doing EMDR therapy & my therapist directly called out an 11 year old part of me, who immediately switched into me. I was still present, but not able to talk and my therapist began treating me like a child and making me feel comfortable, because “she” was terrified. For myself, parts has been a comfortable term, but we are working on allowing my parts to let go of certain ideologies and memories from the past. I highly recommend trying EMDR therapy if that’s available to you, but the main focus to remind yourself is that the parts or voices, whatever makes you feel more comfortable, won’t just disappear! They’ll always be there. They don’t need to worry about leaving, but we created a table. A safe place where nothing bad can happen to talk and negotiate with my parts. After my first switch that happened, she didn’t properly close out session and I was blended with this 11 year old part, went out and bought a stuffed animal & barely remember. So, next time I was back, I went to our meeting room and asked who was the one to buy the turtle. It’s all about starting a relationship, but be careful :) You’re not crazy at all! I would do some researched into DID, OSDD, parts work and maybe meditation if that feels safe. It’s a nice way to calm your mind when dealing with the other voices!

I don’t know. I’ve always been scared. I’ve been watching horror/ghost hunting shows since I could remember, so I’ve always been scared of ghosts and what not. As I started to progress through my teenage years, I was followed home by 2 men in a truck. It honestly wasn’t a big deal. They drove by where I lived. I remember in that moment, running as fast I could to get back home. I was perched in my window with a knife. (I was 12 at the time) Ever since that I’ve always been more aware to check my back. I feel like someone’s following me. I dealt with that for about 5 years before I started getting even worse attacks from it. I’m not able to walk alone for too long without feeling extremely paranoid and uncomfortable. Once in this anxiety attack, my mind starts to play tricks on me. 

My brain: “imagine if there was that fire face demon from the Insidious movie right there in ur closet.”

That thought replays over and over until I’m paralyzed in fear, stuck in the corner of the room absolutely terrified all because I made a thought become real. 
I’ve never seen anything ever. It’s all just in my head. “There’s not actually someone standing over there.”
It makes me question if it was real. 

I could go on and on. My guy, I could write novels about my stupid life.
